questions.q: A large artery has numerous concentric elastic lamellae throughout its tunica media. Which vessel is most likely represented?
questions.explain: Elastic arteries such as the aorta contain many elastic lamellae in the tunica media, allowing expansion during systole and recoil during diastole.

questions.q: Which histological feature is most characteristic of a muscular distributing artery?
options: A prominent internal elastic lamina and smooth-muscle-rich tunica media
Numerous elastic lamellae throughout the media
A wall consisting only of endothelium and basal lamina
A very thick tunica adventitia with longitudinal smooth muscle as its defining feature
questions.explain: Muscular arteries have a conspicuous internal elastic lamina and a tunica media dominated by multiple layers of smooth muscle, which regulate regional blood flow.

questions.q: A capillary in skeletal muscle has endothelial cells joined by tight junctions and a continuous basal lamina. Which type is this?
questions.explain: Continuous capillaries have an uninterrupted endothelial lining and continuous basal lamina; they occur in muscle, lung and much of the connective tissue.

questions.q: Which capillary type is specialised for rapid exchange in endocrine glands and intestinal mucosa because its endothelial cells contain pores?
questions.explain: Fenestrated capillaries contain endothelial pores that facilitate rapid fluid and small-solute exchange; they are common in endocrine glands, intestinal mucosa and renal glomeruli.

questions.q: In a section of ventricular myocardium, which specialised cardiac muscle cells conduct impulses rapidly through the subendocardial region?
questions.explain: Purkinje fibres are large, pale-staining modified cardiac myocytes located mainly in the subendocardial layer; their abundant glycogen and specialised gap-junction coupling support rapid conduction.
